tasks.title: Measure where a layer apply spends its time and recommend fixes
tasks.notes: Investigation, not optimisation: change no behaviour. A trees+decor redo of one cell took ~16 min (trees ~13 min for 1308 fills / 9265 blocks, decor ~3 min for 612 fills / 2533 blocks); the process used under a minute of CPU early on, so the wait looks like MCP round trips, but this is inference, not measurement. Add stage timings (surface warm-up, planning, fills, readback, journal writes) to the layer apply output or report, run on one already-built cell under the lock via redo_layer, with enough runs to show variation (state how many). Deliverable: a short finding in rules/slow-commands.md with measured stage times, plus a ranked list of fixes with estimated savings (candidates, untested: merge adjacent boxes into larger fills, fewer and larger readback scans, avoid re-reading surface already probed). Do not start a fix here; file one task per fix that the numbers justify. Do not run while another apply holds the site lock. Related: #222 (counts reporting), #223 (redo_layer).

tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.title: Share residential frontage surfaces, boundaries and access between ground and decor
tasks.notes:
Covers Suburban streets lack distinct frontages, boundaries and entrance connections (I-042), sparse Kitchener Road snag (S-073), southampton-build. Owner approved diagnosis, inference preference and this independently reviewed task on 2026-11-01.
Cause: ground.classify uses map/aerial colours and generic shade filling without garden plot or entrance intent; guessed lawn near any road/building can become paving. garden_sources already grows approximate plots and consumes street/per-property boundary conventions, but Kitchener's convention has selected hedge vetoes and no front fence/wall specification. Boundary generation reserves no entrance gaps or connections. The saved decor report consists of aerial hedges and mapped iron bars. Unverified: exact plots/gates and how many visible columns the paving conversion caused.
Deliver one shared residential frontage description consumed by the existing ground and decor passes: private frontage extent/surface, boundary segments, entrance opening and connection. Reuse existing plots/segments and convention files; no new pass or parallel geometry engine. Use lib/site/provenance.py and existing evidence IDs, retaining property/street scope and reason for inference through plans/reports. Replace the lossy garden tuple/provenance conversion and superseded access-blind joining path.
Evidence: explicit property observation > street-run evidence > labelled deterministic same-street inference. Owner prefers a coherent realistic street from best available evidence over leaving gaps because exact detail is uncertain. Inferred private frontages require identified residential properties and supporting frontage/street evidence; missing conventions alone do not authorize fences. Explicit open frontages, none vetoes and per-house overrides win. Do not randomize surfaces for variety. Retain observed gravel/paving/green differences and distinguish private frontage from public pavement; constrain generic guessed-lawn conversion accordingly. Nonresidential/campus behaviour must remain compatible.
Pass responsibility: feature owns the building/porch, threshold and feature-generated external landing/steps/supports, even outside the mapped footprint. Keep existing placement and journal ownership semantics. Expose a small shared read-only entrance-approach description: actual door, feature approach extent, usable outward connection point/height/direction, clearance and provenance; distinguish generated door positions from observed ones. Ground owns remaining frontage/pavement surfaces and onward route, joining the outer end of the feature approach (door when no approach), without duplicating or replacing feature steps. Decor owns boundary/furniture/gate placement and preserves the route/opening/headroom; it does not construct a second threshold, stair or path. Respect existing trees.
Solid feature steps/landings/supports retain journal ownership. Required clear space is shared semantic planning data, not ownership of air: preserve journal CANCEL/air-cancels rules. Ground/decor must not fill reserved clearance or replace feature solids. Reserve access across mapped, convention, designer and aerial candidates AND final join_pieces/straightening. Explain conflicts with explicit observed boundaries rather than silently erasing them. Preserve lidar heights, masks, ownership, clipping and undo. Blocked connections report endpoints, responsible pass and reason; do not bypass protected blocks or alter the house to force access.
Legacy approaches: use narrowly scoped read-only reconstruction from the landed plan/journal where trustworthy; otherwise label generated/inferred data and unavailable endpoints. A plausible inferred entrance may guide the frontage but cannot be reported as a verified connection to an actual door. Refresh the approach description from current geometry after feature rebuilds; avoid stale copied endpoints. No broad feature/staircase redesign, ownership migration or generic reapply/provenance/cross-cell policy change.
Scope: lib/sources/garden_sources.py, lib/layers/ground_layer.py, decor_plan.py, decor_layer.py and their existing tests; narrowly scoped approach description in lib/builds/house_build.py and feature_build.py plus existing plan/journal metadata only as needed; rules/frontage-and-evidence.md and rules/handoff-layered-passes.md. Keep existing convention files readable. World evidence/data changes and live rebuilds are separate. Do not include other sessions' uncommitted work.
Verification: synthetic partial-evidence residential strip, marked inference, per-house none/override, ineligible no-evidence property, mixed surfaces, gap surviving final joins, path joining an existing stoop, blocked-access report, diagonal/cell-edge and campus regression. Feature generates external steps plus cleared headroom; reload the landed journal/plan (air has no owner), then ground/decor preserve identical feature solids and reserved headroom including final joins. An updated feature approach changes its connection description without changing unrelated readiness policy. Missing legacy endpoint is explicit. Tests use disposable synthetic inputs, never world data. No live apply in tool task.
Separate world review after tool delivery: record best available street/aerial evidence and rebuild 53,-43 ground then decor, feature only if its own approach is faulty. Compare supplied reference camera for public/private separation, boundary openings, and connections to actual visible doors without duplicate/overwritten steps. Inspect evidence/inference reporting; owner judges coherent realism, not exact gate accuracy. Tool task can finish on synthetic checks; I-042 remains open for rebuild and owner verdict. Log the merged fix with issues.py fix and a check line for S-073.
Independent review: revised to reuse existing provenance, protect openings through all sources/final joins, bound residential inference, qualify blocked connections and separate world review; second fresh review clarified semantic clearance versus ownership of air. Priority medium, complexity L, no mandatory blockers. Coordinate shared files with layer reporting (#222); tree rooting (#226), cross-cell policy (#234), angled glazing (#235), legacy reapply (#236) are separate.

[Claude Code/Sonnet 5.5] Slice 1 merged 2026-11-07 (b9fa67f): garden_sources.residential_frontage (extent, boundary, opening, route, connection, provenance; residential-only, door observed vs inferred, blocked report), ground keeps private-frontage guessed lawn, decor reserves openings from barriers/furniture/final joins with conflicts reported, read-only house_build.entrance_approach, rules updated. Remaining: ground consuming route/connection to lay the onward path; wiring entrance_approach to real feature builds and landed journals (doors are always inferred today); reserving route and headroom in decor and checking air stays open; surfacing blocked-connection reports in ground/decor reports; trees in routing; replacing lossy garden tuple/provenance conversion and access-blind join path; furniture dropped in an opening not reported; opening empty when the front boundary is an aerial hedge; tests for diagonal/cell-edge, campus, gap surviving final joins, mixed surfaces, stoop join. World review and I-042/S-073 logging unchanged.

[Claude Code/Sonnet 5.5] Slice 2 merged 2026-11-07: landed doors via entrance_approach.entrances_from_blocks and garden_sources.landed_approaches (street-facing door chosen; route starts at outer end of feature steps), ground paves guessed ground on the route (denoise-exempt), decor reserves route and clearance and reports dropped furniture, blocked connections in ground stats. Still open: headroom/air check in the world, tree handling in routing, replacing lossy garden tuple/provenance conversion and access-blind join path, opening empty when the front boundary is an aerial hedge, entrance_approach scan not bounded by footprint in landed_approaches, world review of 53,-43 (needs Minecraft) and I-042/S-073 logging.

tasks.title: Sparse front boundaries in cell 53,-43 (Kitchener and Sirdar roads): walls, fences, hedges and gates
tasks.notes:
Owner review 2026-11-08 of 53,-43 (southampton-build): very little decor outside house fronts. Not measured yet. Related: #240 (shared frontage between ground and decor), snag S-073. Start by measuring decor per frontage against the aerial and street-run convention, then decide whether the cause is the decor layer or missing boundary evidence. Needs a live world to verify. Spun out of #243 (doors, closed).

DIAGNOSIS 2026-11-09 (read-only; decor report highfield_53_m43_decor-report.json + garden_sources.garden_barriers report).
Measure: 59 eligible fronts in the cell (Kitchener 31, Sirdar 28). 26 have no decor at all. 186 of 1,981 front-yard columns carry decor (~9%), all aerial-hedge fragments. Zero walls, fences or gates; zero furniture in the whole cell (furniture 0). Frontage `boundary` is empty on all 59. Sparse is true on both streets equally.
Aerial (reference/aerial/kitchener-z19 mosaic): fronts are not plain. Most have a low pale wall on the pavement line, side dividing walls or hedges, a paved drive or path gap, gravel/lawn with shrubs, some bins.
Where lost: (1) EVIDENCE, the main cause. A front boundary needs a `front` spec in site/gardens/<street>.json or an aerial hedge (hedge_share >= 0.6). kitchener_road.json has only rear/side vetoes, no `front`; sirdar_road.json does not exist. Aerial hedge fired on 12 of 59 front segments; low walls read pale, not green, so the detector cannot see them. (2) Aerial-hedge fronts never feed residential_frontage `boundary`/`opening` (role_spec only), so those hedges get no entrance gap from the opening logic (route columns are still reserved). (3) No source for private-yard furniture: only map furniture and reference/decor-furniture.json (no 53,-43 entry). (4) NOT the cause: layer drops inside fronts are 29 columns (22 against build, 5 above lidar, 2 blocked); route+clearance take 5-11 columns of 14-58 per yard.
Proposed fix: (a) world data, no code: add `front` (low wall, height 1) and `side_front` to kitchener_road.json and a new sirdar_road.json, citing a registered aerial evidence id; per-house `front: none` where the aerial shows an open drive. (b) code, garden_sources.residential_frontage / garden_barriers: pass the resolved front spec (convention or aerial hedge) into the frontage so `boundary` and `opening` are set for aerial hedges too; widen the opening to the drive width where the route meets a paved strip. Tests in lib/sources/test_garden_sources.py: aerial-hedge front gets an opening; convention front wall leaves the route open. (c) owner decision first: whether to add a front-yard furniture convention (bins beside the opening, planters), labelled inference.
Verify: per-front table before/after (decor columns in extent, boundary length, opening present), decor dry run on 53,-43, then an in-world look along both roads.

OWNER DECISION 2026-11-09: a front yard here should have walls, hedges, fences, bushes, ideally flowers, sheds, garages, ponds and gates. Every element still needs aerial or map evidence per property; nothing is scattered by default. Owning layer for each element: walls, fences, hedges, gates = decor (this task: front/side_front conventions, aerial hedge -> boundary and opening, gate block in the opening; gates are not built today, the opening is left as air). Bushes = trees (bush_voxels for small crowns; check whether front-yard shrubs show in the canopy mask or are lost). Flowers = ground foliage (foliage.py flower list; check whether guessed lawn in private frontage gets any). Sheds and garages = outbuildings: cell_features.py leaves them 'to their house plot' and coverage.py lists OUTBUILDINGS, but nothing appears to build them; this is a gap of its own. Ponds = only mapped natural=water polygons become water_body features; garden ponds from the aerial have no source. Split 2026-11-09 (owner agreed): this task keeps walls, fences, hedges and gates. Sheds and garages moved to #251; bushes, flowers and garden ponds moved to #252.

tasks.title: site_lock.run crashes on macOS with PermissionError in its process-group cleanup and leaves the lock held (redo_layer.py)
tasks.notes: Seen 2026-11-09 on every `scripts/redo_layer.py --apply` run after the layers had applied and verified (southampton-build, macOS): traceback ends at lib/site/site_lock.py run(), `os.killpg(process.pid, 0)` in the post-exit grace loop, `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. Only ProcessLookupError is caught, so on macOS (killpg on a group whose leader has exited can give EPERM, not ESRCH) the finally block aborts before the SIGKILL and `release(owner)`. Effects: the lock stays held by the redo-layer-<pid> owner (a later redo on another cell refuses with 'Held by redo-layer-N'), and the command exits 1 although the work succeeded. Workaround: `site_lock.py --world W release redo-layer-<pid>`. Also note `site_lock.py run ... -- redo_layer.py` cannot wrap redo_layer because it claims the lock itself ('Held by claude'). Fix: treat PermissionError like ProcessLookupError in both killpg calls, always reach release(owner) (nest in try/finally), and add a unit test with a mocked killpg raising PermissionError. Consider making redo_layer honour an existing SITE_OWNER instead of claiming a second lock.

tasks.title: house_build.py should refuse a feature-path spec instead of building a broken house
tasks.notes: On 2026-11-09 I rebuilt houses_kitchener_road_w176634502 with house_build.py; its notes say 'FEATURE PATH (scripts/feature_build.py) ... house_build cannot plan low ground' and its spec uses richer keys (storeys, wall, floor, facade_plan) and roof entries as {kind, material} dicts. house_build read the dict as a material, wrote invalid block names and dropped 502 roof positions (readback mismatches), after undoing the good build. Fix: in load_spec/main, refuse (exit non-zero before any undo or apply) when the spec has storeys/facade_plan keys, a roofs value that is not a string, or notes starting 'FEATURE PATH'; name the right builder in the message. Also make readback mismatches fail loudly in the summary line. Test: spec fixture with dict roofs raises. Spun out of #243 (2026-11-09).

tasks.title: element_undo should check cell readiness before undoing a plan that the rebuild will need
tasks.notes: Earlier in #243 I undid houses_sirdar_road_w177806445 and the rebuild was then refused because cell 53,-44 was not ready (needs-prep: validation stale, aerial coverage), leaving the plan undone until tiles were downloaded and cells prepared. Fix: `element_undo.py --apply` (or a wrapper used by rebuild flows) runs `cell_registry check` for every cell the plan touches and refuses, naming the needed `prepare` or aerial step, when any cell is not ready. A `--force` keeps the old behaviour. Test with a fake registry that reports not-ready. Spun out of #243 (2026-11-09).

tasks.title: Record which builder and spec produced each landed house plan so stale or wrong-builder plans can be found and reapplied
tasks.notes: reapply_feature.py refuses plans with no recorded builder, and in #243 I could not tell which of the eight Kitchener/Sirdar plans were built by the old builder, which by feature_build and which by house_build; I found out from spec notes and by watching which houses kept old-style chimneys. Fix: record builder name (house_build, feature_build), builder git SHA and spec hash in the journal entry for each feature plan; add `site_recover.py`-style listing of landed plans whose builder SHA is older than a given commit or whose spec hash changed; let reapply_feature use the recorded builder. Needs a journal schema bump. Spec in docs/plans/. Spun out of #243 (2026-11-09).

tasks.title: Add a landed-door audit script (present, two-high, level with the ground outside) and use it to audit the remaining house plans
tasks.notes: In #243 I measured doors with throwaway scripts in the scratchpad (parse the 'door (x,z)' lines of builder logs, check the lower and upper half, a solid block under the door and two air cells in front). Make it a committed tool: read doors from landed feature plans (garden_sources.landed_approaches or entrance_approach.entrances_from_blocks) rather than logs, report missing, half-height, below-street and blocked doors per plan, exit non-zero on any. Tests on a synthetic world. Then run it over the plans I have not opened (houses_ripstone_gardens_*, houses_sherborne_road, houses_blenheim_gardens_*, houses_brickfield_road_*, houses_upper_shaftesbury_avenue_*) and file rebuild tasks for any that fail; rebuild with the builder the spec names (see its notes). Spun out of #243 (2026-11-09).

tasks.title: Garden planting: front-yard bushes, flowers and garden ponds from aerial evidence
tasks.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-09 (from the front-decor task #244): gardens should have bushes, ideally flowers, and ponds. Check each before building: (1) bushes belong to trees (trees_layer.py makes bush_voxels for crowns below MIN_CROWN_R); measure whether front-yard shrubs seen on the aerial reach the canopy mask in 53,-43 or are lost. (2) flowers belong to ground foliage (foliage.py flower list); measure whether guessed lawn in private frontage gets any, and propose aerial-led flower beds if not. (3) ponds: only mapped natural=water polygons become water_body features (#163); garden ponds from the aerial have no source, so propose one (aerial water-colour patch inside a plot, labelled inference) or confirm none are visible. Keep the door route and frontage opening clear. Verify with per-plot counts before and after and an in-world look.
